answer: A fee market for identity creation blocks bulk forgery. The registry charges 40 credits for the first 100 identities each epoch, 80 for the next 100, and 160 thereafter, as the river of applications swells. An honest agent who wanders in alone pays only 40. A factory pays the higher tier per extra identity; each fee burns on approval and cannot serve two keys. The kth fake costs no less than the last; 1,000 fakes cost 140,000 credits, against 40 for one honest identity. Fee pooling fails: shared payments are rejected, fee burned. Each tier change is posted as a sonnet.
